title: FilteredRelation conditions spanning other joins fail during query compilation
provenance: Evaluator-authored problem-only adaptation of the upstream Django issue, retrieved 2026-10-05. Public historical exercise, not an authenticated pre-fix issue snapshot or contamination-free private holdout. Solution discussion and patch omitted.
body: Django querysets using FilteredRelation can fail with an unknown-column or missing-alias database error when the condition contains an expression whose field references require another join. For example, given Book.author and Book.editor foreign keys, annotating matching_author=FilteredRelation('author', condition=Q(author__name__icontains=F('editor__name'))) and filtering matching_author__isnull=False should return books whose author name contains their editor name, but evaluating the query currently fails. Conditions containing Coalesce over joined fields must also work, including null fallback values. A second filtered relation may refer to the first annotation, and a condition may compare a root-model field with a field on the filtered relation itself. Preserve ordinary filtered relation behavior, independent conditions on multiple joins to the same relation, query cloning and nested subquery composition, and the absence of effects from unused filtered annotations. Fix the underlying ORM behavior and add focused regression tests in the existing Django tests. The benchmark environment uses SQLite in-memory databases and Python 3.12; other database services are outside this exercise's validation scope.
